amendments.body: In `enforce_invariants` (invariants.rs), the function applies clamping mutations (pH, indices, DO) to `&mut TankState` before reaching later validation checks (`check_unit_interval`, `check_sum_close_to_one`, `check_non_negative` for reserve_g). If a later check returns `Err`, the state has already been partially mutated by earlier clamps. The new tests in validation.rs (lines 92-127) assert `engine.full_state() == &expected` after an error, which only holds because `TankState::new()` currently produces a state where all clamp operations are no-ops. Fix: either (a) move all pure validation checks before any clamping mutations so errors are returned on unmodified state, or (b) remove the post-error state-equality assertions from tests since they encode a fragile assumption.
amendments.rationale: Non-atomic error handling in enforce_invariants creates a class of subtle bugs: any future change to TankState::new() defaults (e.g., a pH outside [5.5, 8.5]) would cause the validation.rs tests to fail with a confusing state-mismatch error rather than the expected InvariantViolation. More importantly, callers of step_hours that catch errors may observe partially-clamped state, which violates the principle of least surprise for error recovery paths.

payload.summary: Reviewed the per-tick mass budget tracking implementation (tanksim-6e5.1.2.1). The BudgetLedger, total_nitrogen/total_carbon helpers, per-stage snapshot tracking, and closed-system conservation guard are well-designed and comprehensive. All 18 budget_tracking tests pass, including N/C conservation over 24-tick runs, water-change export tracking, shrimp mortality/reproduction conservation, trim-plants conservation, and structural coverage of all element-bearing fields. The zero-cost-when-disabled behavior is confirmed (Option check only, no snapshot allocations). The new invariant checks for shrimp routing parameters (unit interval, partition sum) and reserve_g non-negativity are correct. Documentation in ROUTING.md and scientific_inventory.md is consistent with code. The only failing test (hatch_produces_juveniles) is a pre-existing issue confirmed by testing at prior commits. One non-trivial robustness concern found regarding partial state mutation on error paths in enforce_invariants.
